strengths: Clear identification and empirical demonstration of the Jensen's Gap problem in PDE-constrained diffusion models, with effective synthetic experiments (MoG, Stokes) illustrating the phenomenon
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8+ PDE benchmarks with multiple metrics, thorough ablations, compute-matched comparisons, and diverse downstream tasks (forward, inverse, reconstruction)
Efficient one-step generation achieving 100-5000x speedup over baselines while maintaining or improving physical constraint satisfaction
Method naturally supports multiple downstream tasks within a single framework, which prior methods do not provide
Thorough appendix with additional ablations on component attribution, diversity preservation, teacher quality sensitivity, architecture robustness, and dynamic weighting
Honest discussion of limitations and acknowledgment that distributional fidelity claims remain empirical
weaknesses: Theoretical justification is limited: Theorems B.1-B.2 rely on simplified assumptions (low-rank Gaussian, diagonal score networks) with significant gap from actual nonlinear PDE problems; no formal proof that final-sample supervision preserves learned distributions

Distributional fidelity claims lack rigor: FPD metric computed on PDE-learned representations rather than verifying overall sample distribution preservation; diversity metrics (Table 7) don't guarantee samples from same distribution

Improvements are modest and inconsistent: Statistical errors (MMSE/SMSE) often similar or worse than teacher; compute-matched gains over DiffusionPDE are limited; PIDDM-1 requires refinement for strong results

Limited novelty: Applies well-established distillation techniques (Rectified Flow, DMD) to a new domain; enforcing constraints on final samples rather than intermediate estimates is relatively straightforward
Overclaimed minimal hyperparameter tuning: λ_train ranges 10-10⁶ across datasets; Figure 3b-c shows noticeable sensitivity; dynamic weighting required for stiff PDEs despite robustness claims

Jensen's Gap demonstration has limitations: MoG experiment is artificial; Stokes experiment shows increased loss but causality not definitively established; could other factors explain the observation?

Incomplete failure mode analysis: Limited exploration of behavior with noisy/approximate PDE operators, when teacher retraining is needed, or scalability to high resolutions (all experiments at 128×128)

Missing implementation details: Computational cost of teacher sampling not detailed; total training time not reported; code availability not mentioned; masking strategy interaction with physics constraints not theoretically analyzed
